subject: Private deployment — network path & streaming SLO checklist (post-demo)
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Ethan Cole <ethan.cole@brightharbor.com>, Priya Reddy <priya@brightharbor.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 05 May 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Private deployment — network path & streaming SLO checklist (post-demo)

Thanks again for the demo time today — really appreciate the context on BrightHarbor's low-latency inference use case. Below is a concise recap of what we scoped during the call and the proposed verification plan to validate the Private/VPC design meets your SLOs.

TL;DR (business SLOs)
- Target p95 generation latency: <= 120 ms (end-to-end, app -> Redwoods inference)
- Target p99 tail latency: <= 450 ms under steady load + spikes
- Sustained throughput target: 200 req/s (text generation, avg prompt 120 tokens)
- Concurrent sessions to support: 120 active streams (long-poll streaming use case)

Network & streaming constraints we surfaced
- Traffic path: BrightHarbor app -> Transit GW (AWS) -> Customer VPC -> VPN/Peering -> Redwood Private compute in customer VPC
- Important: keep per-hop internal latency budget <= 40ms so we can meet p95 at application level
- Streaming protocol: HTTP/2 gRPC or WebSocket (we confirmed both are possible; prefer HTTP/2 for better multiplexing)
- MTU: 1500 preferred; double-NAT or MPLS paths with smaller MTU will need fragmentation testing
- Encryption: TLS termination preferences (you noted desire to keep TLS end-to-end; we support this)

Proposed verification plan (phase-based)
Phase 0 — quick net sanity (2–3 days, remote)
  - iperf3 baseline between app subnet and Redwood egress IPs (3x 5m tests)
  - ICMP and traceroute (from app control plane) to capture hop latency and jitter
  - Verify BGP/TGW or VPN crypto throughput numbers (cpu-bound vs wire-bound)
Phase 1 — tail-latency smoke (1 week)
  - Synthetic traffic generator (we'll provide script) that mirrors your avg prompt size and token cadence; run at 50/100/200 rps
  - Streaming session test: open 120 concurrent streams for 10m and measure p50/p95/p99
Phase 2 — soak and fallback behavior (2–3 weeks)
  - Sustained 200 rps with scheduled bursts to validate autoscaling and model fallbacks
  - Validate KV cache warm-up and prefix caching impact on tail latency

Immediate asks for BrightHarbor (what we need from you)
1) Confirm whether Transit Gateway is in-path or if you will peer directly from app VPC to Redwood VPC. Note exact attachment IDs if TGW in use.
2) Share an egress NAT IP block that Redwood's test probes should hit (or confirm we'll use the egress IPs in the attached doc).
3) Confirm whether TLS offload will be performed in your edge (yes/no). If yes, provide expected TLS TPS and crypto offload targets.
4) Can you run basic iperf3 from the app subnet to the sample egress IPs this week? We included a short script as attachment.

Attachments: brightharbor-slo-matrix.csv (SLO table), vpn-poc-checklist.pdf (P2P/VPN checklist), network-probe-script.sh (probe script)

Next steps
- If you confirm TGW details and provide one egress IP block, Ben and I will schedule the Phase 0 tests (30–45 min coordination + 1hr test window).
- We'll run a short streaming smoke on a Tuesday morning PT to reduce jitter from worldwide traffic.

Thanks — I can be flexible with times next week.

—

Thanks Karthik — this is a great checklist. Quick clarifications from our side: 
1) We plan to put the TGW in-path (TGW attachment IDs will be available Monday). Will that add any additional latency budget you want to account for?
2) Our VPN gateway is an AWS-managed VPN with a crypto throughput of ~1.2 Gbps. The expected sustained traffic is below that, but bursts could push CPU on the customer gateway. Is there a recommended minimum crypto throughput or instance size on your end for the VPN concentrator?
3) Streaming protocol — we prefer WebSocket for this client stack. You mentioned HTTP/2 being preferable; can you confirm parity of tail-latency and reconnection behavior between the two on private deployments?
4) We'll run iperf3 from the app subnet to your egress IPs later today and share results.

Also, do you have a sample traffic generator that produces tokenized payloads similar to what a real client will send? Sending raw JSON TCP traffic won't capture model compute behavior.

– Ethan

Karthik / Ben — forwarding Ethan's clarifications. My notes inline below.

On Thu, May 6, 2027 at 09:24, Ethan Cole <ethan.cole@brightharbor.com> wrote:
> 1) We plan to put the TGW in-path (TGW attachment IDs will be available Monday). Will that add any additional latency budget you want to account for?

TGW: expect ~5–15 ms extra depending on attachment path and route table complexity. Recommend we target an additional 20ms headroom in internal budget while we baseline.

> 2) Our VPN gateway is an AWS-managed VPN with a crypto throughput of ~1.2 Gbps. The expected sustained traffic is below that, but bursts could push CPU on the customer gateway. Is there a recommended minimum crypto throughput or instance size on your end for the VPN concentrator?

VPN concentrator: for our Private deployments we've seen stable results with >= 2 Gbps of crypto throughput headroom and EC2 instance types with AES-NI (c5n/c6i) for any customer-managed gateways. If you're using AWS-managed VPN, validate tunnel CPU during a short 200 rps run. We'll include a note in the POC checklist to capture tunnel CPU.

> 3) Streaming protocol — we prefer WebSocket for this client stack. You mentioned HTTP/2 being preferable; can you confirm parity of tail-latency and reconnection behavior between the two on private deployments?

Protocol parity: both are supported but HTTP/2 gives better multiplexing and lower connection churn. WebSocket parity is fine for p95 but we should validate p99 under connection churn (client reconnects). Add a reconnect pattern to the streaming smoke tests.

> 4) We'll run iperf3 from the app subnet to your egress IPs later today and share results.

Great — once we have iperf output we'll schedule Phase 0. Also ensure MTU and any IPS/IDS are disabled for test window.

Action items I will take: I will update the vpn-poc-checklist.pdf with the TGW headroom note and add the reconnect pattern to the streaming test config. Ben, can you produce the short traffic generator (tokenized payload) and point to it in the Drive link in the doc?

—

If either of those work, confirm the TGW attachment IDs and the egress IP block so Ben can kick off the probe run. Ben will upload the tokenized traffic generator to the Drive link and we will include exact iperf3 commands in the checklist.

One more note: during Phase 1 streaming smoke we will open 120 concurrent streams for 10 minutes and capture a 30s window at 99th percentile for trace-level logs — this will require a short retention exception on the trial traces (we'll keep them for 7 days). If that's OK, we'll proceed.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this validated.
